definition: Very attentive to detail and hard to please about standards.
example: A fastidious host polished every glass before the guests arrived.
nuance: Fastidious can imply demanding standards, especially of cleanliness, taste, or accuracy.
prompt: An editor insists that every citation follow the style guide exactly.
options: The fastidious editor checked every reference and rejected even minor inconsistencies.
The fastidious editor finished quickly by ignoring small inconsistencies.
His fastidious response arrived sooner than anyone expected.
The fastidious meeting about citation rules dragged on until everyone in the office was bored.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: very attentive to detail and hard to please about standards.
Ignoring details conflicts with exacting standards.
Fastidious is not related to being fast.
This confuses the word with tedious; it describes exacting standards, not something dull.

practice.prompt: A teenager sorts the stamps she has saved from old family letters.
options: Maya was so fastidious that she stuffed loose stamps into a shoebox and lost half of them.
Being fastidious, Maya happily kept every stamp she found, even the torn and smudged ones.
Her fastidious collection now fills twelve albums, more than anyone else's in town.
Maya, ever fastidious, rejected any stamp with a bent corner or faded ink.
reasons: Careless storage and lost items show the opposite of close attention to detail.
Someone who is pleased with damaged items is easy to satisfy, not demanding.
Sheer size says nothing about standards; the sentence treats the word as if it meant vast.
Turning away stamps with tiny flaws shows exacting standards that are hard to satisfy.
